q: Lenses produce images similar to images formed by curved mirrors, but they do so by ____ light rather than reflecting it.
e: Lenses bend light by refraction; they do not reflect like a curved mirror. Lenses produce images similar to images formed by curved mirrors, but they do so by refracting light rather than reflecting it.

q: As a preliminary study for refraction through lenses, we first look at refraction at a single ____ surface.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. As a preliminary study for refraction through lenses, we first look at refraction at a single spherical surface.

q: Consider a spherical surface of radius $R$ separating the two ____ 1 and 2.
e: Consider a spherical surface of radius R separating the two media 1 and 2. Media is what this statement is using.

q: The ray incident at the curved surface will be ____ and meet the ray propagating along the axis.
e: The ray incident at the curved surface will be refracted and meet the ray propagating along the axis. Refracted is what this statement is using.

q: The light ray along the axis is incident on the surface normally and hence is not ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The light ray along the axis is incident on the surface normally and hence is not bent.

q: If the rays are ____, then the angles are very small.
e: If the rays are paraxial, then the angles are very small. Paraxial is what this statement is using.

q: From ____ law, $n_1 \sin \theta_1 = n_2 \sin \theta_2$.
e: From Snell's law, n_1 sin θ_1 = n_2 sin θ_2. Snell's is what this statement is using.

q: If an angle is small and expressed in ____, $\sin \theta = \theta$.
e: For a small angle in radians, sin θ equals θ to a very good approximation. If an angle is small and expressed in radian, sin θ = θ.

q: For refraction at spherical surface, the radius $R$ is positive if the surface is ____ toward the object.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. For refraction at spherical surface, the radius R is positive if the surface is convex toward the object.

q: For refraction at spherical surface, the radius $R$ is negative if the surface is ____ toward the object.
e: R is negative when the surface is concave toward the object. For refraction at spherical surface, the radius R is negative if the surface is concave toward the object.

q: A transparent material which can converge (or) diverge rays of light is called a ____.
e: A lens is a transparent body that converges or diverges light. It needs at least one curved face. A transparent material which can converge (or) diverge rays of light is called a lens.

q: A lens has at least one ____ surface.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A lens has at least one curved surface.

q: The distance between centre of a convex lens and its focus is called the ____ length of the convex lens.
e: Focal length is the distance from the lens centre to its focus. The distance between centre of a convex lens and its focus is called the focal length of the convex lens.

q: The distance between centre of a concave lens and its focus is called the focal length of the ____ lens.
e: Focal length is the distance from the lens centre to its focus. The distance between centre of a concave lens and its focus is called the focal length of the concave lens.

q: The power of lens is ____ proportional to the focal length of the lens.
e: Lens power is 1/f. It is inversely proportional to focal length.

q: The image formed at the first surface acts as the ____ for the second surface of the lens.
e: The image of the first surface is the object for the second surface. A virtual object gets a minus sign.

q: Negative sign is inserted because the first image is the ____ object for the second surface.
e: Negative sign is inserted because the first image is the virtual object for the second surface. Virtual is what this statement is using.

q: Considering the lens as a single entity, the object distance for the lens is $u = u_1$ and the image distance is $v = $ ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Considering the lens as a single entity, the object distance for the lens is u = u_1 and the image distance is v = v_2.

q: We define focal length, $f$ of a lens as the image distance when the object is at ____.
e: Focal length is the image distance for an object at infinity. Do not swap object and image here. We define focal length, f of a lens as the image distance when the object is at infinity.

q: Substituting $u = \infty$ and $v = f$ gives the following ____ equation.
e: Substituting u = infinity and v = f gives the following lens-makers' equation. Lens-makers' is what this statement is using.

q: Combining the refraction equation and the lens-makers' equation, we obtain the ____ equation.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Combining the refraction equation and the lens-makers' equation, we obtain the lens equation.

q: The lens equation is the general formula for the ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The lens equation is the general formula for the thin lens.

q: The object distance $u$ and the image distance $v$ are measured from the ____ of the lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The object distance u and the image distance v are measured from the centre of the lens.

q: Distances of real object, real image and real focus are ____.
e: A real image can be put on a screen. A virtual image cannot; the rays only appear to meet. Distances of real object, real image and real focus are positive.

q: Distances of virtual object, virtual image and virtual focus are ____.
e: A real image can be put on a screen. A virtual image cannot; the rays only appear to meet. Distances of virtual object, virtual image and virtual focus are negative.

q: The perpendicular distance measured above the principal axis is positive and that below the principal axis is ____.
e: The perpendicular distance measured above the principal axis is positive and that below the principal axis is negative. Negative is what this statement is using.

q: A transparent material which can diverge or converge rays of light is called a ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A transparent material which can diverge or converge rays of light is called a lens.

q: Generally, lenses are made up of glass with two ____ surfaces.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Generally, lenses are made up of glass with two spherical surfaces.

q: There are two main types of lenses, known as convex (or) converging lens and concave (or) ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. There are two main types of lenses, known as convex (or) converging lens and concave (or) diverging lens.

q: Lenses are used in spectacles, cameras, projectors, telescopes and ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Lenses are used in spectacles, cameras, projectors, telescopes and microscopes.

q: The convex lens (or) converging lens is used as a magnifying ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The convex lens (or) converging lens is used as a magnifying glass.

q: The lenses in spectacles used by a short-sighted person are ____ lenses.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The lenses in spectacles used by a short-sighted person are concave lenses.

q: The lenses in spectacles used by a long-sighted person are ____ lenses.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The lenses in spectacles used by a long-sighted person are convex lenses.

q: A lens which can converge the parallel rays is called a ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A lens which can converge the parallel rays is called a convex lens.

q: A convex lens is thicker in the ____ than at the edges.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A convex lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges.

q: Three types of convex lens are bi-convex, plano-convex and converging ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Three types of convex lens are bi-convex, plano-convex and converging meniscus.

q: A lens which can diverge the parallel rays is called ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A lens which can diverge the parallel rays is called concave lens.

q: A concave lens is thinner in the middle than at the ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A concave lens is thinner in the middle than at the edges.

q: Three types of concave lens are bi-concave lens, plano-concave lens and diverging ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Three types of concave lens are bi-concave lens, plano-concave lens and diverging meniscus.

q: Bi-convex and bi-concave lens are ____ used.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Bi-convex and bi-concave lens are widely used.

q: Each surface of a lens has a centre of ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Each surface of a lens has a centre of curvature.

q: Since a lens has two surfaces it has two centres of ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Since a lens has two surfaces it has two centres of curvature.

q: The line joining the centres of curvature of two surfaces is the ____ axis of a lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The line joining the centres of curvature of two surfaces is the principal axis of a lens.

q: The principal axis passes through the ____ of the lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The principal axis passes through the middle of the lens.

q: If the radii of curvature of the two surfaces of a lens are equal, the lens is said to be ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. If the radii of curvature of the two surfaces of a lens are equal, the lens is said to be symmetric.

q: A point in the middle of a symmetric lens on the principal axis is the centre of a lens (or) the ____ centre of a lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A point in the middle of a symmetric lens on the principal axis is the centre of a lens (or) the optical centre of a lens.

q: The rays parallel to the principal axis converge at a point on the principal axis after refraction through a ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The rays parallel to the principal axis converge at a point on the principal axis after refraction through a convex lens.

q: This point is called the principal focus of the convex lens and is denoted by ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. This point is called the principal focus of the convex lens and is denoted by F.

q: Since these rays actually pass through the focus, the focus of the convex lens is ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Since these rays actually pass through the focus, the focus of the convex lens is real.

q: The distance between centre of a convex lens and its focus is called ____ length of the convex lens.
e: Focal length is the distance from the lens centre to its focus. The distance between centre of a convex lens and its focus is called focal length of the convex lens.

q: The rays parallel to the principal axis are divergent after refraction through a ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The rays parallel to the principal axis are divergent after refraction through a concave lens.

q: Those divergent rays appear to come from a point on the ____ axis.
e: Those divergent rays appear to come from a point on the principal axis. Principal is what this statement is using.

q: This point is called the principal focus of the ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. This point is called the principal focus of the concave lens.

q: Since the divergent rays do not actually pass through that point, the focus of the concave lens is ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Since the divergent rays do not actually pass through that point, the focus of the concave lens is virtual.

q: The distance between centre of a concave lens and its focus is called the ____ length of the concave lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The distance between centre of a concave lens and its focus is called the focal length of the concave lens.

q: The rays parallel to the principal axis enter the convex lens from the left and pass through the focus on the ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The rays parallel to the principal axis enter the convex lens from the left and pass through the focus on the right.

q: If the rays parallel to the principal axis enter the convex lens from the right, they will pass through the focus on the ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. If the rays parallel to the principal axis enter the convex lens from the right, they will pass through the focus on the left.

q: Thus, a lens has two ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Thus, a lens has two foci.

q: Like a convex lens, a concave lens has two focal points or ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Like a convex lens, a concave lens has two focal points or foci.

q: The points at a distance of twice the focal length from the centre of lens are represented by ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The points at a distance of twice the focal length from the centre of lens are represented by 2F.

q: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focus after refraction through a ____ lens.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focus after refraction through a convex lens.

q: A ray parallel to the principal axis is refracted through a concave lens and the refracted ray produced backward passes through the ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A ray parallel to the principal axis is refracted through a concave lens and the refracted ray produced backward passes through the focus.

q: A ray passing through the focus of a convex lens emerges ____ to the principal axis after refraction.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A ray passing through the focus of a convex lens emerges parallel to the principal axis after refraction.

q: A ray passing through the centre of lens emerges in the ____ direction.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. A ray passing through the centre of lens emerges in the same direction.

q: Only two of the principal rays are sufficient to locate the ____ of an object in various positions.
e: Only two of the principal rays are sufficient to locate the image of an object in various positions. Image is what this statement is using.

q: When the object is at infinity, its image is at $F$, real, inverted, and ____ than the object.
e: When the object is at infinity, its image is at F, real, inverted, and smaller than the object. Smaller is what this statement is using.

q: Due to this property, convex lens can be used as object lens of a ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Due to this property, convex lens can be used as object lens of a telescope.

q: When the object is beyond $2F$, its image is between $F$ and $2F$, real, inverted, and smaller than the ____.
e: When the object is beyond 2F, its image is between F and 2F, real, inverted, and smaller than the object. Object is what this statement is using.

q: Due to this property, convex lens can be used in a ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Due to this property, convex lens can be used in a camera.

q: When the object is at $2F$, its image is at $2F$, real, inverted, and of the ____ size as the object.
e: When the object is at 2F, its image is at 2F, real, inverted, and of the same size as the object. Same is what this statement is using.

q: Due to this property, convex lens can be used in a photocopier making ____-sized copy.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Due to this property, convex lens can be used in a photocopier making equal-sized copy.

q: When the object is between $F$ and $2F$, its image is beyond $2F$, real, inverted, and ____ than the object.
e: When the object is between F and 2F, its image is beyond 2F, real, inverted, and larger than the object. Larger is what this statement is using.

q: When the object is at $F$, its image is at ____.
e: When the object is at F, its image is at infinity. Infinity is what this statement is using.

q: Due to this property, convex lens can be used as in a spotlight to produce ____ beam.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. Due to this property, convex lens can be used as in a spotlight to produce parallel beam.

q: When the object is between $F$ and $P$, its image is behind the object, virtual, erect (upright), and larger than the ____.
e: Near 0.01 mm Hg the glass behind the anode fluoresces where the rays hit. When the object is between F and P, its image is behind the object, virtual, erect (upright), and larger than the object.

q: Due to this property a convex lens can be used as a magnifying ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Due to this property a convex lens can be used as a magnifying glass.

q: The image formed by a concave lens is always virtual, erect (upright) and ____ than the object.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. The image formed by a concave lens is always virtual, erect (upright) and smaller than the object.

q: It is formed between $P$ and $F$ on the ____ side of the lens as the object.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. It is formed between P and F on the same side of the lens as the object.

q: Convex lens can produce both real and virtual images depending on the ____ of the object.
e: A real image can be put on a screen. A virtual image cannot; the rays only appear to meet. Convex lens can produce both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object.

q: However, a concave lens can produce only ____ image.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. However, a concave lens can produce only virtual image.

q: The virtual image formed by the convex (or) concave lens is the same size as the object only when the object is in ____ with the lens.
e: A real image can be put on a screen. A virtual image cannot; the rays only appear to meet. The virtual image formed by the convex (or) concave lens is the same size as the object only when the object is in contact with the lens.

q: The magnification is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the ____.
e: Linear magnification is image height over object height, also v/u with signs. The magnification is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object.

q: Magnification is usually denoted by the letter ____.
e: Linear magnification is image height over object height, also v/u with signs. Magnification is usually denoted by the letter m.

q: The power of a lens is inversely proportional to the ____ length of the lens.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The power of a lens is inversely proportional to the focal length of the lens.

q: The power of a lens is denoted by the letter ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The power of a lens is denoted by the letter P.

q: The lens having greater power can make the rays parallel to the principal axis more convergent (or) ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The lens having greater power can make the rays parallel to the principal axis more convergent (or) divergent.

q: The shorter the focal length the ____ is the power of the lens.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The shorter the focal length the greater is the power of the lens.

q: Since the focal length of a convex lens is positive in sign it has a ____ power.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Since the focal length of a convex lens is positive in sign it has a positive power.

q: The focal length of a concave lens is negative so that it has a ____ power.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The focal length of a concave lens is negative so that it has a negative power.

q: The sign of the powers of the lenses used here are the same as those used by the ____ makers.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The sign of the powers of the lenses used here are the same as those used by the lens makers.

q: If a lens has a focal length of 1 metre, it has one unit power (or) one ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. If a lens has a focal length of 1 metre, it has one unit power (or) one dioptre.

q: One unit of power of a lens is denoted by ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. One unit of power of a lens is denoted by D.

q: If the focal length $f$ is measured in metre, the power is $P = $ ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. If the focal length f is measured in metre, the power is P = (1)/(f (m)).

q: If the focal length $f$ is measured in centimetre, the power is $P = $ ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. If the focal length f is measured in centimetre, the power is P = (100)/(f (cm)).

q: If the power of a lens is $+2 \text{ D}$, it is a ____ lens.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. If the power of a lens is +2 D, it is a convex lens.

q: If the power of a lens is $+2 \text{ D}$, its focal length is ____ m.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. If the power of a lens is +2 D, its focal length is 0.5 m.

q: If the power of a lens is $-4 \text{ D}$, it is a ____ lens.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. If the power of a lens is -4 D, it is a concave lens.

q: If the power of a lens is $-4 \text{ D}$, its focal length is ____ cm.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. If the power of a lens is -4 D, its focal length is 25 cm.
